Shape moments playground

1) A shape sheet is synthesized by the 'Draw Shapes' subgraph (ellipse, circle, square, triangle, rotated bar) and measured with 'CV Shape Moments': centroids (red dots), major-axis orientation (yellow segments, only meaningful for elongated shapes - compare the eccentricities text) and the 7 log-scaled Hu invariants.

2) The middle branch renders a ROTATED + SCALED copy of the triangle on its own canvas and finds it on the sheet by Hu-moment distance - moments do not care about pose or size.

3) ...which is a problem when you DO care. Section 3 shows the invariance policy; section 4 shows moments of the image INTENSITY rather than of an outline.

nodes.title: Find the query shape on the sheet

widgets_values:
Asking for LESS invariance

cv2.matchShapes ignores translation, scale and rotation by design, and reflection by accident: only the 7th Hu invariant's sign changes under mirroring, and matchShapes skips any term below its internal eps=1e-5, which |h7| usually is. Measured: the F below and its mirror are indistinguishable (~0), and the mirror can even rank ABOVE a good but rotated shape - while a hook shape with a bigger |h7| scores 0.50. The distance is not a handedness test in either direction. The five matchers below differ only in their scale / rotation / mirror policy widgets, so each one is COLLAPSED with just that widget promoted to a primitive next to it - change the dropdown on the canvas and the matcher follows. Their results are not printed but DRAWN: every matcher outlines what it kept in red on its own copy of the sheet, and the five copies collapse into ONE labelled preview.

The sheet holds an 'F' upright, the same F turned 40 deg, one at 0.6 scale, a MIRRORED one at 25 deg / 0.85 scale, and a square distractor. An F is used because handedness is only measurable on a chiral shape: it reads |chirality| 0.02-0.05 while a square reads exactly 0 and is reported as UNDECIDABLE rather than guessed. Every shape in section 1 is mirror-symmetric, which is why this section needs its own sheet.

'Reference warped onto its mirrored match' proves the recovered pose: the reference outline is pushed through the matcher's own 'transforms' output and lands on the glyph it matched.

nodes.title: Reference warped onto its mirrored match

widgets_values:
4) Moments of the image INTENSITY

cv2.moments takes either a point set or a raster, and the default for a raster is binaryImage=False - the mass of a pixel is its VALUE. That is Hu's original density function, and the contour nodes cannot reach it: they integrate a uniform density inside an outline.

All three disks below have the SAME outline, so 'Filter Contours By Shape' scores them 0.000000 - it is looking at the silhouette, which is identical. 'Match Image Moments' sees the inside and separates the flat disk at ~0.55.

The left- and right-weighted disks are exact MIRRORS of each other, so Hu scores them 0.000000 as well, on this path too - what separates them is the intensity CENTROID (~139 vs ~161). That is the SAME mirror-blindness the contour matcher has, showing up again on the raster path.

The offset lobe also gives these disks a real axis (pose_confidence ~0.022). A FLAT disk is radially symmetric and reads ~0 instead - the node saying it has no orientation rather than inventing one.
